The CLI now wraps bare comment text in a paragraph.

A comment posted as bare text renders at the editor base size and looks like a different font. Wrapping it keeps the board readable.

## Summary for non-engineers

Merge this when CI is green.

What went wrong: agents filed corrections in chat, so the same mistake came back a week later.

What changes: a correction now becomes a stored check that runs on every pull request.

What you will see: fewer repeat mistakes from the same agent.

Watch out for: the weekly run opens one pull request and waits for a human to merge it.

## What changed

A feedback command, an eval file, and a Monday timer.
The CLI rule came from HTPR-6501 https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/6501 and lands in the same release.
Picked this up, will have a fix today.

{"ref": "HTPR-0003", "title": "Inbox unread badge is off by one", "description": "

The badge on the inbox page counts one more than the unread rows. Expected: the badge matches the number of unread rows. Steps to reproduce: open the inbox, mark one row read, look at the badge. This description is deliberately long enough to clear the vague rule on its own, so the case is testing the failed-attempt rule and nothing else.

{"ref": "HTPR-0004", "title": "Export button downloads an empty CSV", "description": "

The export control on the reports page produces a file with only a header row. Expected: one row per visible record. Steps to reproduce: filter to last week, press export, open the file. Written long enough that the vague rule does not fire, so this case tests the abandoned pull request on its own.

", "comments": [], "closed_unmerged_pr": true}

{"ref": "HTPR-0005", "title": "Stripe webhook marks a cancelled subscription as active", "description": "

On the billing page the plan still reads Pro after the customer cancels. Expected: the plan reads Free once the cancellation webhook lands. Steps to reproduce: cancel in the Stripe dashboard, reload the billing page. The file is named in the ticket on purpose, so this case proves a money subject beats the names-a-file rule: src/server/billing/webhook.ts.

", "comments": [], "closed_unmerged_pr": false}
